question: What do Samsung Galaxy S10e reviewers say about using the phone on their carrier network?
answer:
One reviewer reported that their Galaxy S10e was tied to Sprint rather than being Samsung-unlocked, and that it would only connect to certain carriers such as Verizon, T-Mobile and Sprint and possibly AT&T. [65d911be6913_1]
Another reviewer said the phone needed tweaking by the seller and carrier to work on their Straight Talk network, calling setup a bit of a pain but worth the savings. [91d68e4907e1_0]
Other reviewers reported a phone still locked to T-Mobile despite being advertised as unlocked, a phone blocked by a carrier that couldn't register on T-Mobile, a phone that only worked on Wi-Fi and wouldn't connect to a carrier, and repeated network errors with GSM SIM cards. [fea2f19ec1cb_0] [4d874223d3f4_0] [e7d38c338a05_0] [a08f9d1b9276_0]

chunks.text: They combine reviews the actual review for the 256 GB blue phone that you see in the picture is what I am writing right now. That phone is not unlocked it is tied to Sprint it is not Samsung unlocked Samson did not unlock this phone. This is carrier unlocked. So it will not connect to any carrier you want only certain carriers such as Verizon T-Mobile and Sprint and possibly AT&T. I have a prepaid which is called Visible wireless and that will not connect. I have other unlock phones that will work with Visible no problem. This phone has a Sprint rom Meaning by default it is always trying to connect to the sprint network. You can choose another net work manually, but certain carriers will not connect such as visible wireless. I should mention LTE does connect through Visible wireless.

AT&T uses GSM and Verizon uses CDMA so I thought the incompatibility verdict seemed reasonable. In working with the carriers CS agent, he had me go into settings>connections>mobile networks>network mode. There you will see a list with one of the choices checked indicating the setting the phone is on. He told me to select "Global" . When I told him there was no "Global" or "LTE/CDMA" selection, he said the phone was not compatible. Picture 1 is my old S6, which I am replacing, and Picture 2 is the S10e. The CS agent also had me go into the Access Point Names. There was no access point listed, just some text saying "not available to this user" or something similar.

No longer works on network. Bought to replace old phone in August 2021. Everything said it would work on network when they shut down 3G. Come February 2022, carrier says no longer works on network and have to buy a new phone to keep account. I seriously think something should be done about these false advertisers ripping people off.

Unlocked Phone didn't work on AT&T Network. I was under the impression that an unlocked phone worked on any mobile carrier network. I was wrong. Phone didn't connect with my existing Sim card. I called At&t and was on the phone with customer service for an hour and was told that I needed a new Sim card. I went to the At&t store and was provided with a new Sim card. This didn't work either. So after wasting a week waiting for the phone and hours to set it up, ultimately I had to return it. Then I had to wait another week for another phone that did work right out of the box. I also haven't been issued a refund for the item even though it was returned to them (I checked the return and it made it) almost a week ago.

Great phone. The functionality of the phone is fantastic, but the phone needs some tweaking by the seller and your carrier to work on your carriers network (in my case Straight Talk). Getting this phone setup for network and calling was a bit of a pain, but we'll worth the savings of a brand new phone.

Phone was advertised as Unlocked, but was sent a phone still locked to T-Mobile. I guess it's a good thing that's the carrier I needed. Phone is in excellent used condition- which is the reason for the 3 stars. But now I'm out the money I spent on this phone if I ever want to switch carriers. Super deceptive practices, and from the hundreds of reviews saying the same thing, I can see I'm not alone.

When you sell an item make sure everything works before you send it to the customer.. I love the phone! But i couldn't get a sim for it. You need to know before you buy which network your phone will work on. My carrier said this was compatible with my network, but it wasn't. It was a great phone! I would highly suggest this seller! The phone was near perfect and not a scratch!

Phone was blocked. after reading some of the comments before buying I was a little worried. I got the phone it looked great but when I swapped SIM cards it couldn't register on a network and I had T-Mobile. I took it there to see if they could do it. They read the numbers that identified that phone and put it into their system. Turns out the phone was blocked by a carrier. The refund was fast.
Only works on Wi-Fi —won’t connect to carrier. Phone only works with Wi-Fi- will not connect to carrier so it cannot be used.

I've had a difficult time. For me personally, I've had many issues activating with gsm carriers. It definitely is unlocked. As all of these services say my imei is clean. However I think there is an issue with the device because anytime I put in a sim card. Doesn't matter if it's activated in store or not. It comes up with network errors. I'd love to get a replacement and use this device because I'm plenty happy with the product I've gotten from the seller. It just doesn't connect to mobile networks. Which is a stressor on my work. If possible I'd love to update this posting when I can get an available replacement or refund. Again. Not an issue with the seller. I just believe this device has a fault in it. I messaged the seller and we're currently in communication about how to best solve this problem. To sum it up.
